(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE M.G.S.KAMAL) This appeal is by the plaintiff in O.S.No.186/2017 aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 15.09.2021 passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge,
Kalaburagi (hereinafter referred to as 'the Trial Court' for short), by which the trial Court dismissed the suit of the plaintiff with costs.

2. The above suit is filed by the plaintiff against the defendants seeking relief of declaration to declare him NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 to be the absolute owner of the property bearing Sy.No.26/3/A measuring 2 acres 38 guntas now numbered as Sy.No.26/4 situated at Honnakiranagi village (suit property), he having purchased the same from one Saibanna in terms of registered deed of sale dated 29.03.1983.

It is contended that in furtherance to the said deed of sale, the name of the plaintiff was entered in the revenue records and he has been in enjoyment of the same as absolute owner of the same.
3. That the defendant No.3/Special Land Acquisition Officer having acquired the suit property had issued notice under Section 28(5) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act.
Since the land was acquired, the plaintiff is entitled for the compensation payable by the defendant No.3.

However, defendant No.1, who is the wife of the brother of the plaintiff without having any concern with regard to the suit property, with a malafide intention of receiving the compensation in respect of suit schedule property, illegally got her name NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 entered in the revenue records.

Defendant No.1 in collusion with her husband and revenue authorities had created a bogus watani patra and thereby got her name mutated in the revenue records only to defraud and deny the Shanker vs Yashodabai And Ors on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166097299/
2
legitimate right of the plaintiff to receive the compensation in respect of the suit property.

Hence,
the suit.
4. Defendant No.1 appeared and filed written statement admitting the plaintiff purchasing the suit property from one Saibanna under deed of sale dated 29.03.1993.
However it is specifically contended by defendant No.1 that the suit property was purchased in the name of the plaintiff out of the joint family funds.
It is also contended that on the very same day remaining extent of land in the said survey number was purchased in the names of the defendant No.1 and other members of the joint family.
As such it is specifically denied that suit schedule property is the absolute and self acquired property of plaintiff.

Defendant No.1 further contended NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 that there was a partition effected between plaintiff and defendant No.1 in Ugadi of 2009 in terms of which suit schedule property was allotted to the share of husband of defendant No.1 and since the plaintiff himself had given the application to the revenue authorities, name of defendant No.1 was entered into.

It is also contended that in the earlier partition land in Sy.No.362/1/2 and Sy.No.184 were also included and all the joint family properties were divided amongst the plaintiff, Mahadev and daughters of Tukkaram.
That earlier plaintiff had filed suit in O.S.No.257/2013 and he had contended the land in Sy.No.26 to be the joint family property.
Contending as above defendant No.1 sought dismissal of the suit.

5. Trial Court framed following issues and additional issues:
1. Whether the plaintiff proves that, by virtue of registered sale deed, dated 29.03.1993 he alone become absolute owner of suit schedule property?
2. Whether the plaintiff further proves that, defendant No.1 has illegally and fraudulently got entered her name in revenue records pertain to suit property?
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 3.
Whether defendant No.1 prove that, in partition of year 2009, suit property fell to share of her husband?
4. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for reliefs as prayed for?
5. What order or decree?

Additional issues:
1. Whether the plaintiff valued subject matter of suit property for payment of court fee and paid proper court fees accordingly?
6. Plaintiff examined himself as PW-1 and exhibited 28 documents marked as Ex.P-1 to P28.
Defendant No.1 examined her son Ramesh, S/o Mahadevappa as DW-1 and exhibited 21 documents marked as Ex.D1 to D21.

On appreciation of evidence trial Court answered issues 1, 2 and 4 in the Shanker vs Yashodabai And Ors on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166097299/
3 negative and issue No.3 and additional issue No.1 in the affirmative and consequently dismissed the suit with costs.
Being aggrieved by the same, the plaintiff is before this Court.

7. The points that arise for consideration are:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 1.

Whether the trial Court is justified in holding that the plaintiff failed to prove he being the absolute owner of the suit schedule property and that defendant No.1 had obtained her name fraudulently entered into the revenue records?

2. Whether the trial Court was justified in accepting the contention of defendant No.1 that there was family partition in the year 2009 in terms of which the suit property fell to the share of her husband?
8. The case of the plaintiff as seen above is that he is the owner of the suit schedule property having purchased the same under deed of sale dated 29.03.1993 out of his own income.
Said deed of sale is produced at Ex.P1.
Ex.P2 and P3 to P8 are the mutation order and the revenue records reflecting the name of the plaintiff in respect of the suit schedule property.

That apart plaintiff has also produced documents in the nature of `No Due Certificate' issued by Prathamik Sahakara Krushi and Gramina Abhirudhi Bank at Ex.P9 wherein his name has been shown as owner of the suit property.
He has also NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 produced the notice issued by the Special Land Acquisition Officer on 02.07.2013 under Section 28(6) of KIAD Act.
9. In contrast defendant No.1 has specifically contended that suit property was purchased from and out of the joint family income.
As such suit property is joint family property of husband of defendant No.1 and other joint family members.
That in a family partition that had taken place in the year 2009 suit property was allotted to the share of her husband.
10. Before adverting to the rival claims it is necessary to note that plaintiff has been filing one after the other suit prevaricating his stand each case.
He has filed suits in (i)O.S.No.257/2013 (ii)O.S.No.267/2014 (iii)O.S.No.458/2014 (iv) O.S.No.262/2022 claiming 1/3rd share in the family properties.

11. Further contrary to his case of he being the absolute owner of present suit schedule property plaintiff NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 during his cross examination recorded on 16.12.2020 and 20.02.2021 has stated as under:
(a) that his father Tukkaram passed away prior to 1969, leaving behind plaintiff being his elder son and other four children namely Mahadevappa, Seethabai, Sonabai and Heerabai as his heirs.

Shanker vs Yashodabai And Ors on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166097299/
4 guntas was partitioned between him and his brother Mahadevappa.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (c) that he has not done any agricultural activities but he was running a furniture business and that he has not produced licence for doing furniture business and he does not have any such document.
(d) that total extent of land in Sy.No.26/3/A measures 8 acres 38 guntas out of which 2 acre 38 guntas was purchased in his name.
Similarly 2 acres each out of remaining land was purchased in the name of his mother-Ambubai, his sister- Sonubai and in the name of wife of his brother Yashodabai- defendant No.1.
Thus admits that four sale deeds were executed on the very same day.

(e) out of 11 acres in Sy.No.184 an extent of 2 acres 30 guntas was purchased in the name of his daughter-in-law-Kavithabai, 2 acres 30 guntas in the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 name of his daughter- Tulajabai and 2 acres 30 guntas in the name of daughter of his sister Indubai and another 2 acres 30 guntas in the name of his wife's brother's wife -Laxmibai.
(f) that land in Sy.No.362/1/2 is the ancestral property.
He however denies he having filed O.S.No.257/2013 claiming 1/3rd share in all the properties namely said land in Sy.No.362/1/2 and Sy.No.184 and 26.
(g) he however admits his signature on the plaint in said O.S.No.257/2013.
(h) he however admits he having filed another suit in O.S.No.267/2014 which has been transferred to the very same Court where the present suit was being tried.
(j) he admits he having filed suit in O.S.No.458/2014 before the III Additional Civil Judge Court in respect of very same property namely land in Sy.No.26.
(k) he admits that he and his brother Mahadev have separated and land in Sy.No.362/1/2 was divided and he having been allotted 5 acres 20 guntas.
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 (l) he being in possession of land in Sy.No.184 measuring 11 acres and also denies there being a partition in Ugadi 2009 between him and his brother.

(m) that entire extent of 8 acres 38 guntas in Sy.No.26 has been acquired by KIADB in the year 2011 and Ambubai, Sonubai and Yashodabai have received compensation in respect of 6 acres of land and that he has obtained an interim order of stay not to disburse compensation in respect of remaining Shanker vs Yashodabai And Ors on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166097299/
5 land of 2 acres 38 guntas which is the suit property.

(n) in the cross examination recorded on 20.02.2021 he admits that in the year 1980 there was a partition between him and his brother in respect of Sy.No.362/1/2 and that except the said land there is no partition in respect of other properties and in the said partition he was allotted 4 acres 29 guntas of land.
However, he has deposed that he has no document of said partition having been taken place in the year 1980 between him and his brother.

(o) he admits that when the properties were purchased in the name of defendant No.1 and his sister he had paid the money towards consideration and that when the property was being purchased in the name of his sister, mother and defendant No.1 there was no partition between him and his brother.

- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 (p) he also admits that he has not taken any action with regard to mutation of name of defendant No.1 in respect of the suit property.
(q) he admits no property standing in his name or in the name of his daughters had been acquired for the purpose of power plant.
(r) he admits that the land which was allotted to the share of defendant No.1, Ambubai and his sister had been acquired by KIADB.
(s) he admits that towards the land purchased in the name of his mother, sister and brother-Mahadev they had paid the sale consideration.

12. Considering the aforesaid categoric, undisputed and unambiguous admission made by the plaintiff with regard to existence of joint family properties and also his failure to prove the partition of the 1980, and also taking into consideration of the subsequent suit in O.S.No.257/2013 filed by him for partition in which the very same property claimed to be joint family property,
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 trial Court held that the plaintiff failed to show that suit schedule property is his absolute property and dismissed the suit.
13. No grounds made out for interference with the reasons and conclusions arrived at by the trial Court. Points raised above are answered accordingly.
14. Learned counsel for the appellant now furnishes certified copy of the plaint in O.S.No.262/2022 wherein the plaintiff has filed another suit for partition and separate possession in respect of five Shanker vs Yashodabai And Ors on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166097299/
6 items of landed property and one house property and for compensation amount.
The said certified copy of the plaint is taken on record and marked as Ex.C-1 for the purpose of reference.
The contents of the said document would reveal the conduct of the plaintiff who is blowing hot and cold every time in every suit he has filed so far.

15. In the present suit itself he claims to be the absolute owner of the suit schedule property and that - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 there were no other joint family properties while he himself had filed suit in O.S.No.257/2013 claiming the very same property along with other properties to be joint family properties.
The said plaint is marked at Ex.D2.
Though in the cross examination initially plaintiff declined to admit he having filed said suit confronted during cross examination admitted his signature.

The properties of the subject matter of the suit in O.S.No.257/2013 are Sy.No.362/1/2 measuring 11 acres 2 guntas, Sy.No.184 measuring 11 acres and land in Sy.No.26, 8 acres 38 guntas including the land which is the subject matter of the present suit and very relief in the very same suit is for 1/3rd share in the said properties.
16. Learned counsel for the plaintiff at this juncture submits that since the plaintiff has now filed a comprehensive suit in O.S.No.262/2022 he may be given liberty to urge the contentions of present suit in that suit.
17. Plaintiff on the one hand claims himself to be absolute owner of the present suit schedule property and - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9509 that there was no joint family properties, on the other hand by filing the suits as noted above claiming partition and separate possession of his purported 1/3rd share in various properties which according to him are the joint family properties.
Plaintiff is thus abusing due process of law and is misusing the precious judicial time of the Courts by repeatedly filing the suits.
In view of this deliberate conduct of the plaintiff, this Court is of the considered view plaintiff needs to be mulcted with costs.
Appeal is therefore dismissed with cost of Rs.25,000/- payable by the plaintiff to the High Court Legal Services Committee, Kalaburagi Bench, Kalaburagi.
